onion_purple_blotch.hausa_name: Duhun Ganye mai Ruwan Hoda a Albasa
onion_purple_blotch.causes: Prolonged leaf wetness, warm humid nights (21-30°C), and overhead water splashing from rain or watering cans.
onion_purple_blotch.symptoms: Sunken water-soaked lesions turning purple-brown with distinctive concentric rings; yellowing and girdling of leaf shafts.

treatments.mild: Remove infected leaves promptly, weed beds for air circulation, avoid evening irrigation.
treatments.moderate: Spray Mancozeb (2g/L) or copper hydroxide. Add a wetting agent (surfactant) to stick to waxy onion leaves.
treatments.severe: Systemic fungicide treatment (Azoxystrobin or Difenoconazole) and withhold overhead water.

onion_purple_blotch.organic_alternative: Spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or garlic-soap extract at first sign.
prevention_tips: Practice 3-year crop rotation without onions or garlic
Use certified disease-free sets and seeds
Plant on raised ridges or beds with furrow irrigation rather than overhead sprinkling
Cure harvested bulbs in shade until necks are completely dry

onion_thrips.causes: Dry hot weather favors rapid thrips reproduction; weeds around field serve as alternative hosts.
onion_thrips.symptoms: Silvery white patches and streaks on leaves with minute black fecal dots; leaves curl, twist, and wither prematurely.

treatments.mild: Wash foliage with mild soap solution; weed around field borders.
treatments.moderate: Spray neem oil or pyrethrin-based botanical insecticide early in the morning.
treatments.severe: Apply registered insecticide like lambda-cyhalothrin or spinosad; ensure spray reaches inside leaf sheaths.

onion_thrips.organic_alternative: Garlic and hot chili pepper extract spray (steep crushed garlic & chili overnight in water with soap).
prevention_tips: Maintain adequate soil moisture — drought stress worsens thrips damage
Intercrop with companion plants like coriander or carrots
Destroy old crop residues immediately after harvest

rice_blast.causes: Spreads through airborne fungal spores favored by high humidity (>90%), warm temperatures (25-28°C), and excessive nitrogen fertilization.
rice_blast.symptoms: Diamond or spindle-shaped grey lesions with dark reddish-brown margins on leaves; brown rot at the neck of the panicle.

treatments.mild: Remove and destroy infected leaves. Improve drainage and avoid excess urea application.
treatments.moderate: Spray approved fungicide (e.g., Tricyclazole 75% WP) in early morning. Drain excess standing water.
treatments.severe: Immediate fungicide treatment within 24 hours to protect remaining panicles. Alert extension workers.

rice_blast.organic_alternative: Spray fermented buttermilk + neem leaf extract, or Trichoderma viride seed treatment.
prevention_tips: Use blast-resistant certified seed varieties
Avoid over-application of nitrogen/urea fertilizer
Maintain balanced plant spacing for ventilation
Practice crop sanitation and weed control

rice_brown_spot.causes: Favored by nutrient-deficient soils (especially low potassium or micronutrients), drought stress, and high humidity.
rice_brown_spot.symptoms: Circular or oval dark brown spots on leaves with light yellow halos, resembling sesame seeds.

treatments.mild: Apply balanced potassium and organic compost; ensure regular water level.
treatments.moderate: Foliar spray of Mancozeb or propiconazole at manufacturer recommended rate.
treatments.severe: Combined fungicide spray and soil nutrition correction.

prevention_tips: Ensure balanced N-P-K fertilizer and micronutrients
Treat seeds before sowing
Maintain regular water management without drought shock

rice_leaf_blight.causes: Bacterial infection spread through irrigation water, splashing rain, and typhoons/strong winds.
rice_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked to yellowish stripes along leaf margins that rapidly enlarge, turn whitish-grey, and dry up.

treatments.mild: Drain excess field water for 3-4 days to arrest bacterial multiplication. Do not apply nitrogen.
treatments.moderate: Spray Copper hydroxide or bactericide formulation as recommended by local extension.
treatments.severe: Remove severely wilted plants to prevent spread across the field.

rice_leaf_blight.organic_alternative: Spray cow dung extract filtrate or fresh wood ash dusting.
prevention_tips: Use resistant rice varieties
Clean irrigation canals and remove weeds hosting bacteria
Avoid top-dressing urea during active disease outbreaks

tomato_early_blight.causes: Warm temperatures and alternating wet and dry periods. Overwinters on crop residues.
tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target-board appearance) beginning on lower older leaves.

treatments.mild: Prune infected lower foliage immediately and discard away from field. Water only at soil level.
treatments.moderate: Apply copper-based fungicide or chlorothalonil following label directions.
treatments.severe: Systemic fungicide rotation and aggressive pruning to open the canopy.

tomato_early_blight.organic_alternative: Baking soda spray (1 tbsp per gallon) + neem oil solution.
prevention_tips: Stake and trellis tomato plants to keep leaves off the ground
Apply mulch to prevent soil splashing onto foliage
Rotate crops 2-3 years away from solanaceous plants

tomato_late_blight.causes: Cool, wet, and foggy weather. Spreads rapidly by airborne sporangia and wind-driven rain.
tomato_late_blight.symptoms: Irregular water-soaked greasy lesions on leaves and stems; white mildew underneath in damp weather; dark brown rot on fruit.

treatments.mild: Rogue out affected plants immediately. Stop overhead watering immediately.
treatments.moderate: Apply preventive/curative copper or metalaxyl fungicide immediately.
treatments.severe: Fast harvest of clean mature green fruits; destroy heavily infested vines.

prevention_tips: Avoid planting near old potato patches or cull piles
Ensure excellent row spacing and morning sun exposure
Scout daily during humid or drizzly conditions

tomato_leaf_curl.causes: Transmitted by the sweet potato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Not spread by tools or seed.
tomato_leaf_curl.symptoms: Upward curling and puckering of young leaves, yellow margins, severe stunting of plants, and flower drop.

treatments.mild: Uproot and bury infected plants to remove the virus source. Control whitefly populations.
treatments.moderate: Spray insecticidal soap or neem oil to reduce whitefly vector numbers.
treatments.severe: Remove infected plants; protect nursery beds with fine mesh insect nets.

tomato_leaf_curl.organic_alternative: Yellow sticky traps + 2% neem oil foliar spray targeting leaf undersides.
prevention_tips: Use TYLCV-tolerant hybrid seed varieties
Install yellow sticky cards to monitor whitefly activity
Eradicate alternative weed hosts around field margins

potato_late_blight.causes: Cool, cloudy, wet weather with high humidity.
potato_late_blight.symptoms: Rapidly spreading dark water-soaked leaf spots, white fungal growth under leaves, tuber brown rot.

treatments.mild: Remove initial infected plants. Hill soil well over tubers to prevent spore wash.
treatments.moderate: Apply contact/systemic protective fungicide on 7-day schedule.
treatments.severe: Cut and destroy vines 2 weeks prior to harvest to prevent tuber contamination.

prevention_tips: Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers
Ensure high hilling to shield developing tubers from rain-washed spores
Destroy volunteer potato plants and cull piles

potato_black_scurf.causes: Soil-borne and tuber-borne fungus thriving in cold, wet soils at planting.
potato_black_scurf.symptoms: Hard, irregular black crusts on tuber skins that do not wash off; stem cankers and stunted shoots.

treatments.mild: Harvest tubers as soon as skin sets to reduce scurf accumulation.
treatments.moderate: Treat seed tubers with approved fungicide before planting.
treatments.severe: Do not replant saved tubers showing black scurf.

potato_black_scurf.organic_alternative: Seed tuber dip in Trichoderma suspension.
prevention_tips: Plant tubers in warm, well-aerated soil
Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-host crops like cereals
Thoroughly wash and dry storage areas

maize_leaf_spot.causes: Thrives in warm, humid conditions with extended dew on leaves and minimum tillage where residues remain.
maize_leaf_spot.symptoms: Rectangular tan-to-gray spots bounded by leaf veins; lesions expand and merge, scorching the leaf.

treatments.mild: Scout upper leaves near the ear leaf. Remove lower diseased leaves in smallholder plots.
treatments.moderate: Apply registered triazole or strobilurin fungicide if lesions threaten the ear leaf.
treatments.severe: Plan early harvest if grain is mature; clear stover after harvest.

maize_leaf_spot.organic_alternative: Foliar spray with fermented compost tea or bio-control agents.
prevention_tips: Plant resistant maize hybrids recommended for your ecological zone
Rotate maize with legumes (cowpea, soybean, groundnut)
Manage residue through tillage or livestock grazing

maize_rust.causes: Airborne spores carried on winds, favored by cool to moderate temperatures and high humidity.
maize_rust.symptoms: Small, powdery golden-brown to cinnamon-brown pustules scattered over both leaf surfaces.

treatments.mild: Usually does not cause severe yield loss on mature crops; monitor progression.
treatments.moderate: Fungicide spray if rust reaches top canopy before tassel stage.
treatments.severe: Document damage for farm records; select resistant seed for next season.

maize_rust.organic_alternative: Sulfur dust or neem-based foliar spray.
prevention_tips: Plant rust-resistant certified hybrid maize
Plant early in the season to escape peak spore dispersal
Maintain balanced soil fertility

wheat_rust.causes: Wind-borne fungal spores travelling long distances under favorable moisture and temperature.
wheat_rust.symptoms: Yellow, orange, or reddish pustules in stripes or patches on leaves and stems.

treatments.mild: Scout weekly. Apply protectant fungicide if detected before heading stage.
treatments.moderate: Apply systemic triazole fungicide per label instructions.
treatments.severe: Spray entire field immediately to halt sporulation.

prevention_tips: Always sow rust-resistant varieties
Eradicate alternative barberry/grass weed hosts
Coordinate with regional agricultural extension warnings

wheat_powdery_mildew.causes: Cool, humid weather and dense crop stands with high nitrogen levels.
wheat_powdery_mildew.symptoms: White fluffy powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces that turn greyish-brown with tiny black specks.

treatments.mild: Avoid further nitrogen applications. Open canopy airflow.
treatments.severe: Protect the flag leaf with curative fungicide spray.

wheat_powdery_mildew.organic_alternative: Dilute milk spray (1:9 with water) or potassium bicarbonate spray.
prevention_tips: Avoid high seeding density
Balance nitrogen with adequate potassium and phosphorus
Select resistant cultivars

cotton_bollworm.causes: Lepidopteran pest larvae boring into buds, squares, and developing bolls.
cotton_bollworm.symptoms: Holes bored into squares and bolls, caterpillar frass around entrance holes, flared squares and fallen bolls.

treatments.mild: Hand-pick visible caterpillars in small plots; install bird perches.
treatments.moderate: Apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or neem-based bio-pesticide.
treatments.severe: Apply selective insecticide when pest threshold exceeds 1 larva per 5 plants.

prevention_tips: Plant trap crops like marigold or maize around cotton field border
Install pheromone traps to monitor adult moth flight
Avoid broad-spectrum sprays that kill natural predatory wasps and spiders

cotton_leaf_curl.symptoms: Upward or downward leaf curling, vein thickening, small cup-shaped leaf outgrowths (enations) under leaves.

treatments.mild: Rogue out and destroy infected young plants; control whitefly vector.
treatments.moderate: Spray systemic insecticide for whitefly management.
treatments.severe: Do not save seed from affected plots.

cotton_leaf_curl.organic_alternative: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) + yellow sticky traps.
prevention_tips: Grow CLCuV-resistant cotton varieties
Clean weed hosts (such as Abutilon, Parthenium) around fields
Avoid late sowing which exposes seedlings to high whitefly populations

healthy_leaf.causes: Proper soil nutrition, adequate moisture, balanced sunlight, and effective pest management.
healthy_leaf.symptoms: Vibrant uniform green coloration, smooth texture, intact leaf margins without spots or wilting.

treatments.mild: No treatment needed. Continue good agricultural practices.
treatments.moderate: Maintain routine field scouting and balanced fertilization.
treatments.severe: Maintain clean field perimeter and good water drainage.

healthy_leaf.organic_alternative: Regular application of well-decomposed farmyard manure or vermicompost.
prevention_tips: Follow integrated pest management protocols
Scout fields weekly during cool morning hours
Maintain records of planting, weather, and crop stages
